steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease and flour a 9x13-inch baking pan.
In a large bowl, stir together flour, sugar, cocoa, baking powder, and baking soda. Add oil, milk, eggs, and vanilla; mix until smooth. Stir in hot coffee last. Spread evenly into the prepared pan.
Bake in the preheated oven for 25 to 35 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the cake comes out clean.

raw_recipe.headline: Chocolate Cake
raw_recipe.description: A moist chocolate cake made with cocoa, hot coffee, and vanilla. Top with your favorite vanilla or chocolate frosting for a sweet treat.
raw_recipe.name: Chocolate Cake

review.reviewBody: Moist, delicious, deep dark chocolate cake that's so easy, so quick to whip together I thought surely I must have forgotten something! No changes and no criticisms, so this is the only commentary this recipe needs. I made half a recipe in an 8" round pan and frosted it with "Chocolate Butter-Creme Frosting," also from this site. Definitely pleased. Definitely worth repeating.

The label on a container of Hershey's cocoa powder that I bought yesterday has a startlingly similar recipe on it. It's called "Hershey's 'Perfectly Chocolate' Chocolate Cake." It uses slightly less flour (1¾ cups instead of 2 cups), slightly more baking powder (1½ tsp.), slightly less baking soda (1½ tsp.), 2 tsp. of vanilla extract instead of 1, and it adds 1 tsp. of salt. (Many reviewers here have suggested adding salt.) It also calls for a cup of boiling water rather than hot coffee. The other ingredients match. For the 9x13 version, it suggests a baking time of 35 to 40 minutes. The label also includes a frosting recipe for the cake. (Both recipes are also on their website, with additional instructions for Bundt, 3-layer and cupcake versions.) I suggest dusting the greased pan with cocoa powder instead of flour.

I've made this cake three times now and it is consistently delicious and moist. This last time I mixed in 6oz of frozen semi-sweet chocolate chips after all the other ingredients had been properly blended. When served hot out of the oven the chips are gooey patches of chocolatey goodness. When the cake is completely cooled- overnight or in the refrigerator- the chips will resolidify. My husband loves the texture of the hardened chips inside each bite. I love this recipe because it is as easy as making a box cake and I realistically have all the ingredients on hand at any time. Thank you for sharing.

Came out moist. I added a shot of Frangelico liquor but other wise followed the recipe. The mix is dry before you add the coffee so don’t worry if you have some lumps in it when you first add the wet mix. I over mixed it in the end folding in the coffee. I cut it down the middle and made a 2 layer cake with Frangelico and vanilla bean Chantilly Cream with strawberry slices.

I made this cake for hubby's; it turned out amazing. I used instant espresso coffee and made sure it was hot and added last...made for great flavour. I've been requested by my kids and hubby to make it again!!

I changed up this recipe by adding a teaspoon of salt, two tablespoons of peanut butter powder and replaced the white sugar with organic raw cane sugar. Super moist and was so good, even without any frosting. My wife and kids loved it too!

Kids loved it, but NEEDS only one change, okay maybe two to make it perfect and they're small changes. PLEASE add 1 teaspoon of salt, it should be in the recipe. In reviews, several people said it wasn't sweet enough but what they probably meant was it tasted flat. I reduced the sugar by 2/3 cup and added 1t salt and it was perfect. Salt makes every baked good better. Other changes I made because that's how I roll - half whole grain flour (spelt in this case), heated up cold brew coffee, used almond milk because it's what I had, avocado oil as my oil, used dutch process cocoa, and because I live at 6100 ft, reduced leaveners accordingly. Also, don't overmix. Before adding the coffee, mix it just barely, so that when you've added the coffee, it's still just barely combined. My kids said it was the best chocolate cake we've had in a long time, served with whipped cream and strawberries.
Delicious, moist, easy. Make every year for birthday cakes. I add 1/2 tsp salt but otherwise make as-is. I cook in 2 8-inch rounds for about 25 min and turns out great.
Phenomenal recipe! Cake has a wonderful flavor and texture. Add buttercream frosting and shredded coconut to the cake baked in a bundt pan. You have a holiday or birthday cake everyone will love.
I skip the water and and use 2 cups hot coffee. I dissolve the baking soda in it. Always comes out fantastic.

Totally amazing recipe! I put less sugar (1 cup and a bit), mixed everything with a hand mixer adding ingredients (eggs, then sugar, oil and so on... with coffee last), baked for 25 min, drizzled with chocolate chip/butter glaze. So moist! Will make it again!
Excellent. I made these as cupcakes with peanut butter frosting for senior luncheon. Rave reviews!
I used water instead of milk. It still turned out fabulous!!
It's so good. Best chocolate cake ever

Delicious chocolate cake. It is and has been my go-to recipe for 20+ years. For the frosting, I use cocao powder, powdered sugar, a pinch of salt, 1/4 cup of creamy peanut butter, cream cheese, vanilla and unsalted butter, and milk to desired consistency. Beat it all together with an electric mixer. I realise that the amts. of the ingredients are missing. Just use common sence and it'll be fine.
Easy to make and family loves it
Looked good until I added the cup of hot coffee. Cake would not cook fully through.

I made this cake and it turned out not to sweet not strong over powering cake, it turned out supper moist and very tasty. My changes was 2 teasp. of vanilla, the amount of oil is the same but I used cocnut oil instead, I had no sugar in the apartment so I used Blue Agave, it is very sweet so I used 1C. instead of 2 C. of sugar, I also changed the hot coffee for espresso 2 teasp. keep in mind espresso is strong so stay with the coconut oil which is sweet. The cake tuned out delicious will make again.

This cake was SO easy, and incredibly delicious! It was perfectly moist, and not too sweet. The addition of the coffee gave the cake a very moist texture and rich flavor. I served it with vanilla ice-cream and hot fudge sauce. No frosting, but I sprinkled the top with powdered sugar. I followed the recipe exactly, with the exception of substituting oat milk. Baking time was 35 minutes. Thanks for this great recipe!!
My Grammy gave me this recipe many yrs ago. I make it often.
